field_acl_comment: Read-path field ACL. Per instance ('default' = default instance), per model, exactly one of 'deny' (blacklist) or 'allow' (exclusive whitelist). '*' is a per-instance model wildcard, currently unused. 2026-08-25, Dalton's decision: commercial masking removed, and the wildcard deny on message_ids with it — it was a payload-size guard, not a privacy control, and it protected nothing, since mail.message is fully readable on its own. Explicit field lists remain the right habit behind the Cloudflare WAF. margin, purchase_price, standard_price and partner credit/balance are readable — Purchasing and Accounting need them, and a read-only connection is a reasonable place to get them. What remains is not commercial. hr.employee uses 'allow' deliberately: an exclusive whitelist is strictly stricter than enumerating PII to deny, and it stays safe when Odoo adds new sensitive fields on upgrade. hr.version (Odoo 19 contract/wage model) keeps an explicit deny list because it has no small readable subset. res.partner.bank hides account numbers. res.users.apikeys was also whitelisted for upgrade-safety and was dropped on Dalton's instruction the same day: the model carries exactly seven fields in Odoo 19 — id, display_name, name, user_id, scope, create_date, expiration_date — and no key or key-prefix among them, since Odoo stores the key hashed. Verified against production before removing, so this opened nothing that existed. If a future Odoo adds a key field to that model, this decision needs revisiting, and nothing here will remind you. These three stay masked because every current holder of this connection carries Odoo's Employees/Administrator and Payroll/Officer groups, so Odoo itself would not refuse a payroll read — this file is the only control until SERVICE-USERS.md is applied. Change only via PR.
